messages:
Maya (People Ops): Heads up 1 - offer accepted for Priya (Data Eng). She needs to fly to India next week for a family matter. Wants to keep the agreed start date if possible and onboard remotely. Thoughts on benefits / I-9?
Ravi (Recruiter): She said travel window is ~7days but could slip if passport renewal queue is long. Happy to have her start remotely and do in-person stuff after return.
Janelle (Benefits): Quick question: can we provisionally enroll someone who's not yet I-9ed? Any blackout rules?
Omar (Payroll): We need completed tax forms and bank info to run payroll. I-9 Section 2 requires in-person verification unless candidate is in the US and we use authorized agent. Outside US = must verify when back.
Immigration-Counsel-Bot: Counsel summary: OPT holders may continue employment while OPT valid. Traveling abroad while OPT and without visa stamp risks re-entry delays. COS to H-1 can be filed, but if candidate departs US before adjudication, COS may be denied. Recommend: either delay international travel until after critical steps (biometric/adjudication) or proceed with remote onboarding and plan in-person I-9 upon return. Consider premium H-1 filing if timeline critical.
Maya (People Ops): Two options on the table: A) Keep start date, remote onboarding, backdate benefits when docs are provided. B) Postpone start until in-person I-9 can be done. Which does benefits/payroll prefer?
Janelle (Benefits): We can backdate enrollment to the official start date if enrollment forms are submitted within the 30-day window. It's more admin but doable. No immediate blackout.
Omar (Payroll): Payroll can pay on start date if W-4 and direct deposit provided. If she's physically outside US >183 days we may have tax residency issues, but a 7-10 day trip is fine. I-9 must be completed in person when she returns.
Ravi (Recruiter): Priya replied: she prefers not to delay start and wants benefits effective as of offer start. She can sign paperwork digitally now.
Priya (Candidate): I can start remotely and join all onboarding calls PST. I'll bring all original docs to HR when Im back. Thanks for the flexibility.
Immigration-Counsel-Bot: Draft travel/remote advisory for Priya below. Recommend sending this exactly or with minor edits.
```
Hi Priya,
A few important notes from Redwood immigration counsel:
- Travel while on OPT can increase re-entry risk, especially if visa stamping is needed.
- Carry your EAD card, I-20 with a recent travel signature, and a copy of your offer letter.
- If you keep the start date, benefits can be backdated if enrollment paperwork is completed within 30 days.
- I-9 Section 2 must be completed in person after you return; please schedule an HR visit within 3 business days of arrival.
- If you expect travel delays >2 weeks, notify us so we can evaluate premium filing options.
Best,
Redwood Immigration Counsel
```
Maya (People Ops): Added note: team will provide loaner laptop and VPN on day 1.
Janelle (Benefits): I'll send the enrollment link now; well flag it for backdating and note any dependent enrollment deadlines.
Omar (Payroll): I'll attach the payroll checklist (W-4, direct deposit). Will follow up with Ravi for bank form copy.
Maya (People Ops): Plan for now: proceed with start date, remote onboarding, benefits provisionally enrolled and backdated upon docs, in-person I-9 scheduled after return. If anything changes, update this thread.
Ravi (Recruiter): Priya confirmed travel 06/0206/10 and wants to start 06/05. Sending advisory + onboarding checklist now.
Maya (People Ops): Thanks all 44D. Closing unless a blocker pops up.
